decisive_items: touching an unpasteurized sheep stomach with an injured hand about 1 month earlier
blood cultures grew a Gram-negative bacillus
Contrast-enhanced thoracic magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated an inflammatory lesion of the T9 lamina and a posterior epidural abscess compressing the spinal cord at T9–T10
response.rationale: Exposure to unpasteurized sheep products plus Gram-negative bacteremia and spinal/epidural involvement strongly favor brucellosis; R5C is a broader microbiologic description without the specific zoonotic link.

rejected.why: Negative TB serology and no supporting spans; less likely.
Discitis is a component but not the specific etiologic diagnosis.
Spondylodiscitis is descriptive, lacks the zoonotic exposure specificity.
Osteomyelitis is generic and does not capture the brucellosis clue.
Spinal epidural abscess is a complication, not the underlying cause.
